newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-RFU MAKES NEW OFFER TO ENGLISH RUGBY CLUBS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-RFU MAKES NEW OFFER TO ENGLISH RUGBY CLUBS.

text.p: Twickenham chiefs have made an improved offer to English top rugby union clubs in the hope that their year-long conflict can be resolved.

The Rugby Football Union (RFU) have agreed to a pay-out of 10 million pounds ($16.5 million) in 1998 on top of their earlier offer of eight million pounds ($13.2 million) this year and 10 million pounds in 1997.
The 24 top clubs have also been offered two places on the 18-strong RFU executive committee. If a 12-man management board is formed, they will get one seat.
The English Professional Rugby Union Clubs (EPRUC), which represents senior club sides, are at odds with the RFU over television rights, control of the game and shareout of money.
The RFU's offer comes a day before EPRUC holds its own meeting.

The RFU said on Tuesday: "Our draft agreement is generous, fair and reasonable and represents a proper balance between the EPRUC clubs for autonomy and the RFU's duty to be a proper guardian of the game."
